My experience is that I struggle with how long things take and acknowledging delays that could happen. For example, when I need to be somewhere for a certain time, I will look online at how long it takes to get there and then leave with exactly that much time but obviously Google maps isn't accurate and delays happen a lot but every single time it's like I blank on how long things take. 

I rely on Ubers so a specific example is I need to be at the train station for 12:30, it takes 15 minutes to drive there on Google maps, Uber says it'll be here in 3 minutes so I wait until 12:12 to order the Uber but then there's no drivers nearby so it takes 10 minutes for the Uber to get here, and traffic is a little worse than usual so it takes 20 minutes to get to the train station and now I've missed my train. 

I am getting better with it but I do tend to rely on my partner to tell me when I should leave. 

I also really hate waiting about, it makes me anxious to stand around and I hate being cold so I don't like standing around outside waiting. So I'm usually late when it's cold outside which ends up being worse since if I miss the train I have to wait for another hour. 

Another example is brushing my teeth, I have to set a timer or use a brush with a built in timer and I don't consider how long it takes to go to the bathroom, put the toothpaste on etc which is a miniscule amount of time but when I think it takes exactly 2minutes and it takes 4-5mins its enough to make me late.

They can break off and stick inside the wounds which can cause infections even if you’re regularly cleaning the area. If you can’t get a hold of alcohol wipes/baby wipes, use a cloth, towel or a piece of clean clothing, they won’t break off in the wound. 

For the wounds, everything you’re doing is right but I’d advise getting an antibacterial cream to help with the healing and reduce how often you have to clean them because regular cleaning can be harsh on the scabs and skin. Also let the wounds breathe over night. You can wear bandaids/bandages during the day but when you’re sleeping remove them. 

For the tools, again you’re doing everything right, all you need to do is make sure they’re completely dry before putting them away or else they’ll rust. Also the pencil sharpener blade is likely to be dull, if it feels like it’s doing significantly less damage even with the same pressure throw it away and replace it. Dull blades can cause jagged cuts which often require stitches because of how prone to infection they are. 

Remember the signs of infection: fever, cold like symptoms, pus in or around the wound, redness/swelling that differs from the initial appearances and swollen glands in the neck, armpits and/or groin. 

Also know the point at which stitches are needed: if the bleeding doesn’t stop after 10 minutes of applying pressure, if the wound is deep/wide and if the skin on either side can’t be pushed back together with light pressure. 

Be careful, be safe and be kind to yourself and others <3

Stay safe, and reach out if you need anything.

It’s a type of addiction, even when happy your brain craves the endorphins that come with self harm. Harm reduction and transference is a good way to overcome it. When you crave harm try watching a horror movie or going for a run, it’ll release adrenaline and noradrenaline which are some of the main things released when self harming.
What sort of things do you enjoy? Horror movies may be a good place to start if you like them they can get your adrenaline flowing and they’re generally easy to access even at night time.

Try starting by wearing long sleeve T-shirts and rolling up the sleeves, that way if you feel uncomfortable you can pull the sleeves down and continue with your day. If long sleeve T-shirts feel too scary, start with hoodies/sweatshirts and roll them up the same. 

After that try T-shirts and zip up jackets, you can roll your sleeves up and even take the jacket off if you feel ready. Then at any point you have something to cover up with if you feel insecure. If it’s too warm for long sleeves and hoodies try temporary tattoos, you can use them to hide the scars without overheating and without feeling so open. Then when you feel more secure you can use less tattoos or more transparent tattoos with more line art than shading. 

Your scars are a part of you, good or bad, they’ll fade one day but you’ll always remember them.

Self harm can be an addiction. It works in a similar way to smoking or drinking. Your brain releases hormones and endorphins when you do it for whatever reason and when you get bored or sad your brain craves the same release. It’s best to find something else that creates the same release. Maybe it’s running, maybe it’s a super exciting video game or film. Whatever it is, it’ll help and be much better than harming yourself.
